source: 1968 Chevrolet Chassis Service Manual, Rear Suspension and Drive Line, p.4-5

procedures.title: Rear wheel camber: adjust
steps: Set the rear wheels on an alignment machine and read the camber angle.
Loosen the cam bolt nut at the inner strut rod mount (see figure 8 in the manual).
Turn the cam and bolt until camber is at specification.
Tighten the nut and torque it to specification.

procedures.title: Rear wheel toe-in: adjust
steps: Remove the torque control arm pivot bolt.
Move the torque control arm to get the specified toe-in.
Fill the gap on the side toward the car centerline, between the arm bushing and the inner wall of the frame side member, with shims.
Shim the outboard gap as needed so the stack is solid between the bushing and the frame side member wall.
With the shim stack chosen, fit the pivot bolt and hardened washers, making sure every shim stays in place (see figure 9 in the manual).
Torque the nut to specification and fit the cotter pin; if the hole does not line up at that torque, tighten to the next flat.
notes: Do not use a thicker shim than needed or force shims in on the inner side of the arm; this can shift the toe setting.

procedures.title: Rear wheel bearings: check end play
steps: Raise the rear of the car so the wheels are off the ground.
Bend back the bolt lock tabs and unbolt the outer end of the axle drive shaft from the wheel spindle flange.
Mark the camber cam position on its bracket, then loosen and turn the camber bolt until the strut rod pushes the torque control arm outward.
Swing the loose end of the drive shaft aside to reach the spindle.
Mount dial indicator J-8001 on the torque control arm and rest the pointer on the flange or spindle end.
